main_turf.bias_notes: Anti-clockwise. A flat, well-grassed 1,605m country circuit featuring a very short 280-metre home straight. The short straight creates a strong natural bias toward front-runners ('E') and box-seat stalkers ('P'). Deep closers ('Swoopers') face near-impossible odds if they turn for home more than 3-4 lengths off the lead.
main_turf.post_bias: In 1100m and 1200m sprints, inside barriers (1-4) hold a significant advantage due to the short initial run before the turn into the back straight. Wide draws (7+) face a severe penalty if trapped 3-wide without cover. In 1600m and 2050m races, the backstretch start is fairer, but saving ground around the final turn remains essential.

handicapping_angles.short_280m_straight_leader_boost: Because the home straight is only 280m long, waiting until the 200m mark to make a challenge is usually too late. Aggressively upgrade horses with proven gate speed ('E') and jockeys who make proactive moves prior to the home bend.
handicapping_angles.wimmera_country_class_drop: Upgrade horses shipping in from Tier 1/2 Victorian venues (Sandown, Geelong, Ballarat, Bendigo) into local country benchmark company. City and provincial class drops represent the highest ROI angle at Murtoa.
handicapping_angles.clay_loam_wet_weather_holding: Murtoa's clay loam soil holds up exceptionally well during wet winter meetings (July Marma Cup). When track condition is Soft or Heavy, look for horses with established wet-track form who can handle a chopping surface.
handicapping_angles.wide_draw_trap_in_sprints: In 1100m-1200m sprint events, heavily downgrade wide-drawn horses lacking early gate speed. Getting caught wide on the home turn severely drains momentum prior to the 280m dash.
handicapping_angles.australian_weight_bifurcation: In Victorian Country Benchmark races (BM52-BM70), top-weight horses carrying 60kg+ face a strict penalty (1kg = ~1 length over 280m). In feature Cup races (Murtoa Cup, Marma Cup), prioritize pure class ratings and L400m speed over weight spreads.
